title: Finite reduction of a normalized tower projection
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $T$ a scheme in the same universe, $D$ its abelian coefficient-tower presentation, and $C\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(B_n))$ a normalized tower: every specified derived reduction is invertible [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Let $M,p,\delta$ be any distinguished Roos triangle for the completed evaluations and actual transitions [def-sp-tower-reconstruction-data, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For each positive $m$, the specified adjunct of $p_m$ is an isomorphism $M\otimes_R^L B_m\to C_m$ in $D(B_m)$. No constructibility or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Proof first paragraph through the reduction formula; expanded steps 1--8.

proof.text: Choose compatible flat-term K-flat representatives and their normalized reduction maps, with the completed lift preserving projections. Normalization of C implies the actual chain-level reductions are quasi-isomorphisms.

Delete the finite prefix below m. The coefficient fiber is the smaller coefficient module shifted by one, with transitions given by powers of ell. Tensor with the K-flat levels. Every m successive error transitions vanish; its derived limit is zero. The normalized constant right tower has limit C_m, so the middle Koszul tower has that limit.

The Koszul--Roos comparison identifies the middle limit with restricted finite reduction of M, preserving the mth projection. Its normalized adjunct is spTowerReconstructionMap. Exact scalar restriction detects isomorphisms, yielding the assertion in the finite-coefficient derived category.
